doc_title: Introduction to Trigonometry: Sine, Cosine, Tangent
notes: Lesson introducing the three basic trig ratios (SOH-CAH-TOA). Structure: hook (surveyor using angles) → right triangle labeling → sine definition → cosine definition → tangent definition → SOH-CAH-TOA mnemonic → worked example → calculator use → practice.

units.label: Hook: surveyor measuring height of building (image)
units.content_summary: Photo of a surveyor using a theodolite to measure the angle to the top of a tall building. Caption: 'How can a surveyor find the height of a building without climbing it?'

units.label: Hook explanation (text)
units.content_summary: Explains that trigonometry allows calculation of unknown sides and angles in right triangles using ratios. The surveyor measures an angle and a known distance, then uses trig to find the height.

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Objectives: label sides of a right triangle (opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse) relative to a given angle; define sine, cosine, tangent as ratios; use SOH-CAH-TOA; solve for unknown sides using trig.

units.label: Right triangle labeling diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Diagram of a right triangle with angle θ labeled. Sides labeled: hypotenuse (longest, opposite right angle), opposite (side across from θ), adjacent (side next to θ). Right angle marked with square symbol.

units.label: Sine definition (text)
units.content_summary: sin(θ) = opposite/hypotenuse. The sine ratio compares the length of the side opposite the angle to the hypotenuse. Always between 0 and 1 for angles 0°–90°.

units.label: Cosine definition (text)
units.content_summary: cos(θ) = adjacent/hypotenuse. The cosine ratio compares the length of the side adjacent to the angle to the hypotenuse. Always between 0 and 1 for angles 0°–90°.

units.label: Tangent definition (text)
units.content_summary: tan(θ) = opposite/adjacent. The tangent ratio compares the length of the opposite side to the adjacent side. Can be greater than 1 (when angle > 45°). Note: tan = sin/cos.

units.label: SOH-CAH-TOA mnemonic (image)
units.content_summary: Visual mnemonic card: SOH (Sine = Opposite/Hypotenuse), CAH (Cosine = Adjacent/Hypotenuse), TOA (Tangent = Opposite/Adjacent). Colour-coded and formatted as a memory aid.

units.label: Worked Example 1: find sin, cos, tan for triangle (text)
units.content_summary: Given right triangle with legs 3 and 4, hypotenuse 5, angle θ opposite leg 3. Find sin(θ)=3/5=0.6, cos(θ)=4/5=0.8, tan(θ)=3/4=0.75. All three ratios calculated and verified.

units.label: Worked Example 1: triangle diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Labeled diagram of the 3-4-5 right triangle from Example 1. Sides labeled with numbers, angle θ marked, right angle indicated. Reference for the calculation.

units.label: Worked Example 2: find unknown side using sin (text)
units.content_summary: Problem: angle θ=30°, hypotenuse=10. Find the opposite side. Solution: sin(30°)=opp/10; opp=10×sin(30°)=10×0.5=5. Shows calculator usage: sin(30) = 0.5. Full worked solution.

units.label: Calculator tips for trig functions (text)
units.content_summary: How to use a scientific calculator: ensure mode is DEGREES not radians; press SIN/COS/TAN then angle value; use inverse functions (sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹) to find angles from ratios.

units.label: Application: surveyor problem solution (text)
units.content_summary: Returns to opening surveyor problem. Given: angle of elevation=60°, horizontal distance=50m. Find building height using tan(60°)=height/50; height=50×tan(60°)=50×1.732=86.6m. Closes the lesson narrative.

units.label: Practice problems: trig ratio calculations (text)
units.content_summary: Five practice problems: write sin, cos, tan for given triangles; find unknown sides given angle and one side; find angle given two sides using inverse trig.
